rochefoucauld.1.meaning: What we call virtue is often just a mix of actions and interests that luck or effort happens to arrange. People aren't always brave out of courage or faithful out of principle; circumstances and self-interest do much of the work.
rochefoucauld.1.today: Much good behaviour is situational. That's humbling, and a reason to design good situations.
rochefoucauld.1.you: Don't rely on people's virtue alone in your teams and systems. Arrange circumstances so good conduct is the easy path.

rochefoucauld.19.meaning: We all have strength enough to bear other people's misfortunes.
rochefoucauld.19.today: It's easy to be philosophical about someone else's suffering. The test comes when it's ours.
rochefoucauld.19.you: Before offering advice to someone struggling, remember how much harder it is from the inside.

rochefoucauld.26.meaning: Neither the sun nor death can be looked at steadily.
rochefoucauld.26.today: Some realities are too bright to stare at directly. We glance, look away, and get on with living.
rochefoucauld.26.you: Practising memento mori doesn't mean staring at death all day. Brief glances each morning are enough.

rochefoucauld.49.meaning: We are never as happy or as unhappy as we imagine.
rochefoucauld.49.today: Psychologists call it affective forecasting error: we overestimate how much events will change our mood.
rochefoucauld.49.you: When you're dreading or craving an outcome, remember: it won't make you as unhappy, or happy, as you think.

rochefoucauld.89.meaning: Everyone complains about their memory; no one complains about their judgement.
rochefoucauld.89.today: We admit small faults readily to avoid admitting larger ones. Blind spots are invisible by nature.
rochefoucauld.89.you: Ask a trusted colleague where your judgement, not your memory, has been off lately. Listen.

rochefoucauld.116.meaning: Nothing is less sincere than asking and giving advice. The asker pretends to defer, but really wants approval and someone to share the blame. The adviser pretends to be disinterested, but usually seeks his own glory or advantage.
rochefoucauld.116.today: Advice-seeking is often validation-seeking. Being honest about that improves the advice.
rochefoucauld.116.you: Before asking for advice, ask yourself whether you want counsel or cover. Then give advice without self-interest.

rochefoucauld.139.meaning: So few people are good company because almost everyone thinks more about what they want to say than about answering what's been said. Even clever, polite people only seem to listen, while their eyes show they're waiting to speak.
rochefoucauld.139.today: Most of us listen to reply, not to understand. Real listening is rare and deeply valued.
rochefoucauld.139.you: In your next conversation, don't plan your reply while the other person speaks. Just listen, then answer.

rochefoucauld.149.meaning: Refusing praise is only a wish to be praised twice.
rochefoucauld.149.today: False modesty is a subtle form of vanity. Graciously accepting a compliment is more honest.
rochefoucauld.149.you: Next time you're praised, just say thank you. Resist the fishing that deflecting invites.

rochefoucauld.215.meaning: Perfect courage and utter cowardice are both rare; most courage lies between them, and it varies as much as faces do. Some are brave at the start of a battle and falter later; some are brave until they've earned a reputation; some face swords but fear gunfire.
rochefoucauld.215.today: Courage isn't all or nothing. People are brave in some situations and not others.
rochefoucauld.215.you: In defence and leadership, understand the specific courage each person has, and don't assume it transfers.

rochefoucauld.218.meaning: Hypocrisy is the homage vice pays to virtue.
rochefoucauld.218.today: Even pretending to be good admits that goodness matters. Hypocrites prove the standard is real.
rochefoucauld.218.you: When you spot hypocrisy, including your own, treat it as a signal of the standard. Then close the gap.

rochefoucauld.233.meaning: There are many hypocrisies in grief. Sometimes, weeping for someone dear, we're really weeping for ourselves: the loss of their good opinion, our comfort and our pleasure. So the dead get credit for tears shed for the living.
rochefoucauld.233.today: Grief is partly self-concern. That's human, not shameful, but worth recognising.
rochefoucauld.233.you: If you grieve, allow the self-concern in it without judgement. Honesty about grief helps it heal.

rochefoucauld.320.meaning: Praising rulers for virtues they don't have is a way of insulting them safely.
rochefoucauld.320.today: Flattery can be a coded rebuke, highlighting what the flattered person lacks.
rochefoucauld.320.you: Listen carefully when people praise leaders for qualities they plainly lack. It may be a message.

rochefoucauld.404.meaning: Nature seems to have hidden talents deep in our hearts that we don't know we have. Only passions can bring them to light, sometimes with more truth and perfection than training could.
rochefoucauld.404.today: Strong motivation reveals abilities we didn't know we had.
rochefoucauld.404.you: What are you passionate about outside work? It may be revealing a talent your career hasn't used.

rochefoucauld.438.meaning: We would want very few things if we clearly knew what we wanted.
rochefoucauld.438.today: Much desire is confused. Clarity about what we really want cuts down our wanting.
rochefoucauld.438.you: Write down the three things you most want this year. Notice how much else becomes less urgent.

rochefoucauld.448.meaning: When luck hands us a great position suddenly, without preparing us for it, it's almost impossible to fill it well and appear worthy of it.
rochefoucauld.448.today: Sudden promotions are hard to grow into. Preparation makes authority feel earned.
rochefoucauld.448.you: Prepare now for the role above yours, so if it comes suddenly you're ready to fill it well.

rochefoucauld.487.meaning: Our peace of mind depends less on the big things in life than on how well or badly we arrange the small things of everyday life.
rochefoucauld.487.today: Daily routines, small frictions and tiny habits shape our mood more than big events do.
rochefoucauld.487.you: Fix one small daily friction this week: a cluttered desk, a bad morning routine. Your calm depends on it.
